# Synthetic NEAR v2 envelope vectors

`browser-v2.json` contains only invented text and deterministic test key material.
The all-zero/incrementing-style seeds are synthetic authority, not provider
credentials or recorded operator state. None of these keys may authorize a live
request or become an admitted code policy.

The vectors were generated by executing the envelope helpers `Ue`, `Re`, `yr`
and `_r` from the publicly deployed privateinference.gg browser asset on
14 October 2026 UTC:

- URL: <https://privateinference.gg/chat/js/browser-xfq6xewy.js>
- SHA256: `b2b1d0220cb838b9bc82baed08b1e845429632aad63c70274cc99485b6b4c49f`
- Consumers: `test/native.test.mjs` and maintenance generator
  `test/reference-vectors.mjs`.

The generator selects the original source between `var hr=Y.encode(` and
`var Se=` and evaluates it in a restricted VM with explicit cryptographic
imports. This tests the deployed helper's key conversion, HKDF info, envelope
layout and UTF8 interpretation, not an independently rewritten wire algorithm.
The bindings use the pinned Noble 2.4.0 primitives: the upstream older curve
conversion accepted a hex public key, so that primitive argument is adapted to
bytes. Both helpers consequently share a cryptographic primitive dependency;
these vectors are interoperability evidence, not an independent cryptographic
implementation or a hardware/provider audit.

The generation check opens the upstream helper's envelopes with this package
and opens this package's fresh envelopes with the upstream helper. The normal
suite decrypts the fixed upstream vectors and refuses tampered envelopes.
Unicode, empty text and a JSON native-tool argument are covered. The full browser
bundle and helper source are not published here; only synthetic generated bytes
are retained.

The upstream bundle carries Noble crypto MIT notices. This package imports
pinned MIT-licensed `@noble/curves`, `@noble/ciphers` and `@noble/hashes`; their
licenses remain in the installed packages. The generated fixture contains no
copied upstream implementation. First-party package and maintenance-test code
use the repository MIT license.
